provenance: Original practice questions, not official or recalled past papers. Use alongside full-length mocks.

questions.q: In C, what is 7 / 2 when both operands are int?
questions.e: Integer division discards the fractional part; a floating operand would change the operation.

questions.q: C: int x=4; int y=x++; What are x and y afterwards?
questions.e: Post-increment yields the old value and then increments x.

questions.q: C: int x=4; int y=++x; What are x and y afterwards?
questions.e: Pre-increment increments first and yields the new value.

questions.q: C: char s[]="SEBI"; What is sizeof(s)?
questions.e: The array contains four characters and a terminating null byte.

questions.q: C: int a[5]; What does sizeof(a)/sizeof(a[0]) give in the same scope?
questions.e: The array total size divided by one element size is the element count. This fails after array-to-pointer parameter adjustment.

questions.q: Which C expression has undefined behaviour?
o: Reading a[4] from int a[5] after initialisation
questions.e: Valid indices are 0 through 4. Out-of-bounds access is undefined.

questions.q: What must a recursive function have to terminate on intended inputs?
o: A reachable base case and progress toward it
questions.e: A base case is insufficient if recursive calls never move toward it.

questions.q: C++: int x=2; int& r=x; r=8; What is x?
questions.e: r is an alias for x. Assigning through r updates x.

questions.q: What does encapsulation primarily support?
o: Controlling access to state through an interface
questions.e: Encapsulation groups state and behaviour and controls how state is accessed.

questions.q: Two methods with the same name but different parameter lists demonstrate what?
questions.e: Overloading distinguishes callable signatures; overriding replaces inherited behaviour.

questions.q: Java: int[] a={1,2}; int[] b=a; b[0]=9; What is a[0]?
questions.e: Both references point to the same array object. No copy was made.

questions.q: What does a Java finally block generally provide?
o: A way to ignore all exceptions
Cleanup executed when leaving the try/catch flow
questions.e: Finally is for cleanup; abnormal VM termination is an exception to the usual execution rule.

questions.q: Python: a=[1,2]; b=a[:]; b.append(3); What is len(a)?
questions.e: Slicing copies the outer list; appending to b does not append to a.

questions.q: Python: a=[[1]]; b=a[:]; b[0].append(2); What is a?
questions.e: A shallow copy shares the nested list, so mutating that nested object is visible through both.

questions.q: What is Python len(set([1,1,2,3,3]))?
questions.e: A set contains only distinct values: 1, 2 and 3.

questions.q: Which structure naturally implements breadth-first traversal?
questions.e: BFS processes discovered vertices in first-in-first-out order.

questions.q: Which structure is used for matching nested parentheses?
questions.e: Each closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket.

questions.q: Binary search requires what property of its search space?
o: An ordered or monotonic search condition
questions.e: It discards half the space based on an order or monotonic predicate.

questions.q: What is the worst-case time of binary search on a sorted array?
questions.e: The remaining interval is halved on each step.

questions.q: Inserting at the head of a singly linked list, given the head, takes what time?
questions.e: Only the new node link and the head pointer need updating.

questions.q: Which traversal of a BST with distinct keys gives ascending order?
questions.e: Left subtree, root, right subtree follows the BST ordering invariant.

questions.q: A min-heap guarantees which relationship?
o: Every left child is less than every right child
Each parent is no greater than its children
questions.e: The heap invariant is local parent-child order, not total sorted order.

questions.q: Building a binary heap bottom-up from n values takes what time?
questions.e: Most nodes are near leaves and require little work; the sum of sift-down costs is linear.

questions.q: A hash table has n entries and m buckets. Its load factor is?
questions.e: Load factor measures entries relative to capacity or bucket count.

questions.q: Which sorting algorithm has O(n squared) worst case despite O(n log n) average behaviour?
questions.e: Repeatedly highly unbalanced partitions make quicksort quadratic.

questions.q: A stable sort preserves what?
o: The original order of all items
questions.e: Stability is useful when composing sorts on multiple keys.

questions.q: What property commonly makes dynamic programming useful?
questions.e: DP stores subproblem results and combines them according to a recurrence.

questions.q: For 0/1 knapsack, can an item be chosen repeatedly?
o: Only when its value is even
questions.e: 0/1 means each item is either selected once or not selected.

questions.q: With coins 1, 3, 4, how many coins optimally make 6?
questions.e: 3+3 uses two coins. Greedy 4+1+1 uses three and is not optimal here.

questions.q: How many overlapping occurrences of ABA are in ABABA?
questions.e: Matches start at zero-based positions 0 and 2.

questions.q: What is the zero-based row-major offset of element [2][1] in a matrix with 4 columns?
questions.e: Offset = row*columns + column = 2*4+1.

questions.q: Which is valid JSON?
questions.e: JSON needs quoted keys, lowercase literals and no trailing comma.

questions.q: Dijkstra’s standard correctness guarantee requires which edge-weight condition?
questions.e: Negative edges can invalidate the greedy finalisation step.

questions.q: A topological ordering exists for which directed graphs?
questions.e: A directed cycle prevents an ordering with every edge going forward.

questions.q: Which key uniquely identifies a row and is selected as the principal identifier?
questions.e: A primary key is the chosen candidate key and disallows null values.

questions.q: Which relational operation selects rows satisfying a condition?
questions.e: Selection filters rows; projection selects attributes.

questions.q: SQL: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
questions.e: WHERE filters input rows, while HAVING filters grouped results.

questions.q: SQL: What does COUNT(column) exclude?
questions.e: COUNT(column) counts non-null values; COUNT(*) counts rows.

questions.q: SQL: What predicate correctly tests a null value?
questions.e: SQL uses three-valued logic; ordinary comparison with null is unknown.

questions.q: Which join retains every left-table row even when there is no right match?
questions.e: A left outer join supplies nulls for the missing right-side values.

questions.q: How does UNION differ from UNION ALL?
o: UNION always sorts by the first column
questions.e: UNION has distinct semantics. Ordering is not guaranteed without ORDER BY.

questions.q: A transaction should happen entirely or not at all. Which ACID property is this?
questions.e: Atomicity prevents partial transaction effects from being committed.

questions.q: Which ACID property concerns persistence after commit?
questions.e: Committed changes should survive the failures covered by the system guarantees.

questions.q: For BCNF, every nontrivial functional dependency X → Y must satisfy what?
o: Y is always a primary key
questions.e: BCNF requires every determinant of a nontrivial dependency to be a superkey.

questions.q: Which index structure is especially suitable for ordered range scans?
questions.e: Sorted leaf entries and leaf links allow efficient range traversal.

questions.q: What does a window aggregate usually preserve compared with GROUP BY?
o: Only one row in the result
questions.e: A window computes over related rows without necessarily collapsing them into grouped rows.

questions.q: Which OSI layer handles routing between networks?
questions.e: The network layer deals with logical addressing and routing.

questions.q: Which transport protocol provides ordered reliable byte-stream delivery?
questions.e: TCP uses sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmissions.

questions.q: What service usually resolves hostnames to IP addresses?
questions.e: DNS provides name resolution; DHCP supplies network configuration.

questions.q: How many total IPv4 addresses are in a /26 subnet?
questions.e: There are 6 host bits, so 2^6 = 64 total addresses. Traditional usable-host count is 62.

questions.q: An Ethernet switch normally forwards frames using which address?
questions.e: Layer-2 switches use their learned MAC forwarding table.

questions.q: What is ARP used for in an IPv4 LAN?
o: Resolving a local IPv4 address to a link-layer address
questions.e: ARP maps an on-link IPv4 destination or next hop to its MAC address.

questions.q: Which protocol is associated with sending email?
questions.e: SMTP transports outgoing mail. POP3 and IMAP are mainly for mailbox access.

questions.q: What does TCP flow control mainly protect?
o: The receiver from excessive incoming data
questions.e: The receiver window limits how much unacknowledged data the receiver can accept.

questions.q: Which CIA property is harmed when unauthorised users read confidential records?
questions.e: Confidentiality controls disclosure to unauthorised parties.

questions.q: A record is altered without authorisation. Which CIA property is directly affected?
questions.e: Integrity concerns correctness and unauthorised modification.

questions.q: Which combination represents two distinct authentication factors?
questions.e: Knowledge plus possession is multifactor. Two knowledge secrets are the same factor type.

questions.q: Which control most directly prevents SQL injection in query parameters?
questions.e: Bind values as data rather than concatenating them into executable SQL.

questions.q: Passwords should generally be stored using what?
o: Reversible encryption with a shared hardcoded key
questions.e: A deliberately costly password hash with a unique salt limits offline guessing and precomputed attacks.

questions.q: A digital signature is typically created with which key?
questions.e: Verification uses the corresponding public key. Signing does not itself encrypt the message.

questions.q: Which policy best follows least privilege?
o: Grant only necessary access and review it
questions.e: Limit access by role and task, and review it as needs change.

questions.q: What distinguishes an IPS from a purely passive IDS?
o: An IPS can actively block traffic
questions.e: An intrusion prevention system can intervene; detection alone alerts.

questions.q: Python: list(range(1,6,2)) gives what?
questions.e: range excludes the stop value and advances by the supplied step.

questions.q: In pandas, which selector is primarily position-based?
questions.e: iloc selects by integer positions; loc uses labels or boolean masks.

questions.q: A join key appears 3 times on the left and 2 times on the right. How many matching rows can an inner join produce for it?
questions.e: Every left match combines with every right match: 3*2 rows.

o: An error because indexing starts at 0
questions.e: R uses one-based vector indexing.

questions.q: R: mean(c(2,NA,6), na.rm=TRUE) gives what?
questions.e: Removing the missing observation leaves (2+6)/2 = 4.

questions.q: Which ETL stage standardises inconsistent date formats?
questions.e: Transformation cleans and maps source values into the target representation.

questions.q: Moving from daily totals to monthly totals is which OLAP operation?
questions.e: Roll-up aggregates to a coarser level of a hierarchy.

questions.q: What should a fact table’s grain define?
questions.e: A clear grain prevents mixing measures at incompatible levels of detail.

questions.q: Which regex matches exactly three ASCII digits and nothing else?
questions.e: Anchors require the whole string and {3} sets the exact repetition count.

questions.q: In a shell script, what does $# represent?
questions.e: The argument count is separate from $1 (first argument) and $? (previous status).

questions.q: Which shell exit status conventionally indicates success?
questions.e: Zero means success by convention; nonzero usually signals failure.

questions.q: What does a shell pipe connect?
o: Left command stdout to right command stdin
questions.e: A pipe streams one program’s standard output to another’s standard input.

questions.q: Why quote "$name" in a shell command?
o: To preserve it as one argument despite spaces
questions.e: Double quotes allow variable expansion while preventing word splitting and pathname expansion of the result.

questions.q: Why commonly run sort before uniq?
questions.e: Identical lines must be adjacent to be consolidated by uniq.

questions.q: What is a primary market transaction?
o: An issuer selling newly issued securities
An investor reselling existing shares on exchange
questions.e: The primary market raises funds through new issuance; secondary trading transfers existing securities.

questions.q: What does diversification mainly reduce?
questions.e: Combining imperfectly correlated exposures can reduce concentration risk, but does not guarantee returns.

questions.q: An equity share generally represents what?
questions.e: Equity is a residual ownership claim with uncertain returns.

questions.q: What is a depository’s core role?
o: Holding securities electronically and facilitating transfers
questions.e: Electronic holdings and book-entry transfers are central depository functions.

questions.q: Which instrument gives its holder a right, without an obligation, to buy at a specified strike under its terms?
questions.e: A call provides the purchase right; a put provides the sale right.

questions.q: What does a mutual fund NAV represent?
questions.e: NAV divides the fund’s net asset value by its outstanding units.

questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
o: Each of the applicant are ready.
Each of the applicants are ready.
Each of the applicants is ready.
questions.e: Each is the singular subject; the phrase of the applicants does not change agreement.

questions.q: Choose the correct usage.
o: The results affected to the decision.
questions.e: Affect is the verb meaning influence; results is plural and takes affect.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to mitigate?
questions.e: Mitigate means make less severe; it does not mean eliminate.

questions.q: Which sentence uses parallel structure?
o: The role requires analysis data, to write reports and controls.
The role requires analysing data, writing reports and reviewing controls.
The role requires analysing data, reports written and review.
The role requires analyse data, writing and controls.
questions.e: All three coordinated activities use the same grammatical form.

questions.q: All A are B. Some B are C. Does some A are C necessarily follow?
questions.e: The B-C overlap may be entirely outside A.

questions.q: A > B and B >= C. What follows?
questions.e: Combining a strict greater-than with a non-strict greater-than gives a strict greater-than.

questions.q: A candidate ranks 7th from the top and 14th from the bottom. How many candidates are there?
questions.e: Add the two ranks and subtract one to avoid counting the candidate twice.

questions.q: A person walks 6 km east then 8 km north. What is displacement magnitude?
questions.e: The straight-line displacement follows the Pythagorean theorem: sqrt(36+64).

questions.q: A value rises 20% then falls 20%. Relative to the original, it is now?
questions.e: Multipliers 1.2*0.8 = 0.96. The percentage changes have different bases.

questions.q: A does a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. Together they need?
questions.e: Combined daily work rate is 1/10+1/15 = 1/6.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. One is drawn uniformly. P(blue) is?
questions.e: Two of the five equally likely outcomes are blue.

questions.q: How many ways can 2 people be selected from 5, ignoring order?
questions.e: 5 choose 2 = 5*4/2 = 10. Divide by two because each pair can be ordered in two ways.

questions.q: A train covers 150 km in 2.5 hours. Average speed is?
questions.e: Average speed = total distance divided by total time.

questions.q: Python: total=0; then for i in range(3): total += i. What is total?
questions.e: range(3) includes 0 through 2. Their sum is 3*2/2.

questions.q: An item costs Rs 300 and is sold at a 20% profit on cost. What is the selling price?
questions.e: Selling price = cost * 1.20 = 300 * 1.20.

questions.e: Selling price = cost * 1.20 = 1600 * 1.20.

questions.q: Which scheduling algorithm provably gives the minimum average waiting time?
questions.e: SJF is optimal for average waiting time, but it needs burst times in advance, which is why it is not directly implementable.

questions.q: Belady's anomaly can occur in which page replacement algorithm?
questions.e: FIFO can produce more page faults with more frames. LRU and Optimal are stack algorithms and are immune.

questions.q: How many child processes are created by three successive fork() calls?
questions.e: 2^n - 1 children for n sequential forks, so 2^3 - 1 = 7.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four Coffman conditions for deadlock?
questions.e: The four are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. Priority inversion is a separate scheduling problem.

questions.q: In the Banker's algorithm, an unsafe state means:
o: Deadlock is possible but not certain
questions.e: Safe implies no deadlock, but unsafe only means deadlock could occur; it is not a guarantee.

questions.q: A logical address space of 4 GB with 4 KB pages needs how many bits for the page offset?
questions.e: Offset bits = log2(page size) = log2(4096) = 12.

questions.q: Thrashing is best described as:
o: A process spending more time paging than executing
questions.e: It happens when a process has too few frames for its working set, usually from too high a degree of multiprogramming.

questions.q: Which disk scheduling algorithm gives the most uniform waiting time?
questions.e: C-SCAN services in one direction then jumps back without serving, so requests at both ends wait similarly.

questions.q: A binary semaphore differs from a mutex mainly because:
o: A mutex has ownership; only the locking thread may unlock
questions.e: Ownership is the key distinction; a semaphore may be signalled by any thread.

questions.q: Threads of the same process share all EXCEPT:
questions.e: Each thread has its own stack, registers and program counter; everything else is shared.

questions.q: Which scheduler controls the degree of multiprogramming?
questions.e: The long-term (job) scheduler decides how many processes enter the ready queue.

questions.q: A system call is best classified as:
questions.e: System calls are synchronous software-generated traps that switch the CPU to kernel mode.

questions.q: A process that has terminated but whose parent has not called wait() is called:
questions.e: The entry remains in the process table until reaped. An orphan is one whose parent died first.

questions.q: In Round Robin with n processes and quantum q, the maximum time a process waits before its next turn is:
questions.e: Every other process runs at most one quantum before the turn comes back.

questions.q: RAID 5 can survive the failure of how many disks?
questions.e: RAID 5 uses distributed single parity. RAID 6 with dual parity survives two.

questions.q: The range of an 8-bit two's complement number is:
questions.e: Two's complement is asymmetric and has a single zero.

questions.q: In IEEE 754 single precision, the exponent field is how many bits and what is the bias?
questions.e: Single precision is 1 sign + 8 exponent + 23 mantissa, bias 127.

questions.q: Which pair of gates is functionally complete (universal)?
questions.e: Any Boolean function can be built from NAND alone or NOR alone.

questions.q: Overflow in two's complement addition occurs when:
o: Operands of the same sign give a result of the opposite sign
questions.e: Adding two positives giving a negative (or vice versa) signals overflow.

questions.q: A 2^n-to-1 multiplexer can implement any Boolean function of how many variables directly?
questions.e: With n select lines it covers all 2^n minterms; with one inverter it can stretch to n+1 variables.

questions.q: Cache mapping with exactly one possible line per block is:
questions.e: Direct mapping needs no replacement policy because there is only one candidate line.

questions.q: Average memory access time equals:
o: Hit time + miss rate x miss penalty
questions.e: AMAT = hit time + (miss rate x miss penalty), applied recursively for multi-level caches.

questions.q: Which cache miss type is reduced by increasing associativity?
questions.e: Conflict misses come from too many blocks mapping to one set; fully associative caches have none.

questions.q: In a k-stage pipeline executing n instructions, the ideal speedup approaches:
questions.e: Speedup = nk/(k+n-1), which tends to k for large n.

questions.q: A RAW hazard is:
o: A false dependency removable by renaming
questions.e: Read-after-write is a genuine dependency; WAR and WAW are name dependencies fixed by register renaming.

questions.q: With a 32-bit address bus and byte addressing, the addressable memory is:
questions.e: 2^32 bytes = 4 GB. The address bus width alone fixes the addressable range, independent of how much RAM is installed.

questions.q: Which addressing mode is most natural for accessing array elements?
questions.e: Base plus index maps directly onto array indexing; PC-relative suits branches.

questions.q: Gray code is characterised by:
o: Exactly one bit changing between successive values
questions.e: Single-bit transitions avoid intermediate glitches in encoders and K-map adjacency.

questions.q: A mod-12 counter requires at least how many flip-flops?
questions.e: A mod-N counter needs ceil(log2 N) flip-flops, so ceil(log2 12) = 4. Four flip-flops give 16 states, of which 12 are used.

questions.q: In a Moore machine the output depends on:
questions.e: Mealy outputs depend on state and input and usually need fewer states, but can glitch.

questions.q: Which SDLC model pairs every development phase with a corresponding test phase?
questions.e: The V-model maps requirements to acceptance testing, design to integration testing and code to unit testing.

questions.q: Which model is explicitly risk-driven?
questions.e: Boehm's spiral model devotes one quadrant of every loop to risk analysis.

questions.q: Cyclomatic complexity of a program with 10 edges, 8 nodes and 1 connected component is:
Good software design aims for:
questions.e: Modules should be internally focused and externally independent.

questions.q: Which type of coupling is the worst?
questions.e: Content coupling means one module modifies another's internals. Data coupling is the best form.

questions.q: In COCOMO, which mode has the highest effort exponent?
questions.e: Embedded projects have the tightest constraints, with b = 1.20 against 1.05 for organic.

questions.q: The PERT expected time for an activity is:
questions.e: The beta-distribution weighting gives the most likely estimate four times the weight.

questions.q: Activities on the critical path have:
questions.e: The critical path is the longest path through the network and determines project duration.

questions.q: Verification answers which question?
o: Are we building the right product?
Are we building the product right?
questions.e: Verification is process conformance; validation checks fitness for user needs.

questions.q: Which maintenance category is typically the largest share of effort?
questions.e: Enhancement and improvement dominate, at roughly half of maintenance effort.

questions.q: Top-down integration testing requires:
questions.e: Stubs stand in for lower modules; bottom-up integration needs drivers instead.

questions.q: Boundary value analysis for a valid range of 1 to 100 should test:
questions.e: Defects cluster at boundaries, so test just inside and just outside each edge.

questions.q: In Scrum, who owns the product backlog?
questions.e: The Scrum Master serves the team and removes impediments but does not own the backlog.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four DORA metrics?
questions.e: The fourth is mean time to restore. LOC per developer is a discredited productivity proxy.

questions.q: CMMI level 5 is:
questions.e: The ladder is Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, Optimising.

questions.q: Which HTTP methods are idempotent?
questions.e: Repeating a PUT or DELETE has the same effect as doing it once; POST and PATCH do not guarantee that.

questions.q: HTTP 401 versus 403 means:
questions.e: 401 asks you to identify yourself; 403 says who you are is not allowed.

questions.q: Which cookie attribute is the primary defence against CSRF?
questions.e: SameSite stops the cookie being sent on cross-site requests. HttpOnly mitigates XSS theft instead.

questions.q: The most reliable fix for SQL injection is:
questions.e: Parameterisation separates code from data so input can never be parsed as SQL.

questions.q: XSS exploits trust in which direction?
o: The site's trust in the user's browser
The user's trust in the site
The server's trust in the database
questions.e: CSRF is the mirror image: it exploits the site's trust in the user's browser.

questions.q: HTTP/3 runs over which transport?
questions.e: QUIC removes TCP head-of-line blocking and speeds up connection setup.

questions.q: REST's statelessness constraint means:
o: The server stores no session state between requests
questions.e: Each request carries all context needed, which is what allows horizontal scaling.

questions.q: The top-ranked API vulnerability in the OWASP API list is:
questions.e: BOLA/IDOR: failing to check that the caller may access the specific object identified in the request.

questions.q: CORS is best described as:
o: A browser-enforced relaxation of the same-origin policy
questions.e: It loosens, not tightens, the default restriction, and only browsers enforce it.

questions.q: In Kubernetes, the smallest deployable unit is:
questions.e: A pod holds one or more containers that share network and storage.

questions.q: Which deployment strategy exposes a small percentage of traffic to the new version first?
questions.e: Blue-green switches all traffic at once between two full environments.

questions.q: Availability of 99.9% allows roughly how much downtime per year?
questions.e: 99.99% is about 52 minutes and 99.999% about 5 minutes.

questions.q: RPO measures:
o: How fast service must be restored
How much data loss is tolerable
questions.e: RTO is time to restore; RPO is the acceptable data-loss window, set by replication design.

questions.q: Which pattern stops an application repeatedly calling a failing dependency?
questions.e: The breaker opens after repeated failures and fails fast until the dependency recovers.

questions.q: Containers isolate workloads using:
o: Namespaces and cgroups on a shared kernel
questions.e: That shared kernel is also why a container is a weaker security boundary than a VM.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the five essential characteristics of cloud computing in NIST SP 800-145?
questions.e: The five are on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity and measured service.

questions.q: In IaaS, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system?
questions.e: In PaaS and SaaS the provider handles it; identity configuration and data always stay with the customer.

questions.q: The most common root cause of publicised cloud data exposure is:
questions.e: Public storage buckets and over-permissive IAM roles dominate real incidents.

questions.q: For a financial-sector regulator, the biggest systemic cloud concern is:
o: Concentration risk across a few providers
questions.e: If most regulated entities depend on the same provider or region, one outage becomes a market-wide event.

questions.q: In HDFS, the default replication factor is:
questions.e: Three replicas by default, with the NameNode holding metadata as a single point of failure.

questions.q: MapReduce phases in order are:
questions.e: Shuffling and sorting group values by key between the map and reduce stages.

questions.q: Apache Spark is faster than MapReduce for iterative work mainly because it:
questions.e: In-memory RDDs avoid writing intermediate results to disk on every pass.

questions.q: For a fraud model with 0.1% positives, which metric is most misleading?
questions.e: Predicting 'no fraud' always would score 99.9% accuracy and catch nothing.

questions.q: L1 regularisation (Lasso) is notable because it:
o: Drives some coefficients to exactly zero, selecting features
questions.e: L2 (Ridge) shrinks coefficients without eliminating them.

questions.q: Overfitting corresponds to:
questions.e: The model memorises noise in training data and generalises poorly.

questions.q: In a blockchain, tampering with one transaction is detectable because:
o: It changes the Merkle root and therefore every subsequent block hash
questions.e: Hash chaining plus the Merkle tree makes any alteration propagate visibly.

questions.q: For regulated securities-market use, the realistic DLT choice is:
o: A permissioned ledger with known participants
questions.e: Permissioned ledgers with BFT consensus give deterministic finality and identifiable parties.

questions.q: Atomic delivery versus payment (DvP) removes which risk?
questions.e: Both legs settle together or not at all, so neither side can deliver without receiving.

questions.q: Shor's algorithm, if run on a large quantum computer, would break:
questions.e: Grover's algorithm only halves effective symmetric key strength, so AES-256 remains adequate.

questions.q: 'Harvest now, decrypt later' refers to:
o: Recording encrypted traffic today to decrypt when quantum capability arrives
questions.e: It is why migration to post-quantum cryptography and crypto-agility starts before the threat is live.

questions.q: Which set makes up Market Infrastructure Institutions?
o: Stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories
questions.e: MIIs are systemically important and are governed largely by the SECC Regulations, 2018.

questions.q: Novation by a clearing corporation means it:
o: Becomes the buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer
questions.e: Acting as central counterparty is what removes bilateral counterparty risk.

questions.q: An exchange order book is ordered by:
questions.e: Price-time priority: the better price wins, and at equal price the earlier order wins.

questions.q: Market data feeds often use UDP multicast rather than TCP because:
o: One publisher must reach many subscribers simultaneously and fairly
questions.e: Sequential unicast would advantage whoever is served first; order entry still uses TCP.

questions.q: SEBI's regulatory concern about co-location is primarily:
o: Equal and non-discriminatory access to the same facilities and data
questions.e: Hence equal-length cabling, transparent allocation and access for smaller members.

questions.q: Placing orders with no intention of executing them, to move prices, is:
questions.e: Spoofing and layering are manipulative practices actionable under the PFUTP Regulations.

questions.q: Detecting circular trading among connected accounts is most naturally modelled as:
questions.e: Accounts are nodes and trades or fund transfers are edges; look for cycles and communities.

questions.q: The difference between RegTech and SupTech is:
o: RegTech serves regulated entities; SupTech serves the supervisor
RegTech is hardware, SupTech is software
RegTech is Indian, SupTech is global
questions.e: A SEBI IT officer works on the SupTech side, supervising entities that rely on RegTech.

questions.q: Under the PIT Regulations, the Structured Digital Database must record:
o: Persons with whom unpublished price sensitive information is shared, with time stamps
questions.e: It must be non-tamperable and maintain an audit trail - an explicitly technological obligation.

questions.q: ASBA in a public issue means the application money is:
o: Blocked in the investor's own bank account until allotment
questions.e: UPI provides the retail block mechanism; the funds are debited only on allotment.

questions.q: Which KYC body is specific to the securities market?
questions.e: CKYCR is sector-wide across finance; KRAs are SEBI-registered for the securities market.

questions.q: For market systems, the expected disaster recovery posture includes:
o: A DR site in the same building
A DR site in a different seismic zone with live drills
Annual paper review of the plan
questions.e: Intraday recovery timelines and periodic live drills, including member participation, are expected.

questions.q: Cyber recovery differs from ordinary disaster recovery because:
o: It must assume the primary environment is compromised, not merely unavailable
It only applies to small firms
questions.e: Replication faithfully copies corruption, so immutable backups and rebuild are required.

questions.q: Clock synchronisation across trading systems matters because:
o: Order and trade timestamps must be comparable for audit and surveillance
questions.e: Without a common time reference, surveillance replay and glitch investigation are meaningless.

questions.q: DDPI replaced the broad power of attorney model in order to:
o: Narrow the authority a broker holds over client securities
questions.e: It followed misuse of client securities held under wide POAs.

questions.q: Which property is provided by a digital signature but NOT by a MAC?
questions.e: A MAC uses a shared key, so either party could have produced it.

questions.q: To encrypt a message so only the recipient can read it, you use:
questions.e: Sign with your private key for authenticity; encrypt with their public key for confidentiality.

questions.q: Which block cipher mode should never be used for bulk data?
questions.e: ECB encrypts identical plaintext blocks to identical ciphertext, leaking structure.

questions.q: AES has a block size of:
questions.e: Key sizes vary at 128, 192 or 256 bits, but the block is always 128 bits.

questions.q: For n users, symmetric cryptography requires how many keys for pairwise secure communication?
questions.e: Asymmetric cryptography needs only 2n keys, which is why key distribution drove its invention.

questions.q: Passwords should be stored using:
o: A salted, deliberately slow KDF such as bcrypt or Argon2
questions.e: Salting defeats rainbow tables and slowness defeats mass offline cracking.

questions.q: Which is genuine multi-factor authentication?
o: Password plus OTP on a registered device
questions.e: MFA requires different factor types: something you know, have or are.

questions.q: A lower Crossover Error Rate in a biometric system indicates:
questions.e: CER is where false acceptance and false rejection rates meet; lower is better.

questions.q: OAuth 2.0 is fundamentally a framework for:
questions.e: OpenID Connect adds the authentication layer on top with an ID token.

questions.q: Under the CERT-In directions of April 2022, specified cyber incidents must be reported within:
questions.e: The same directions require 180 days of ICT log retention within India.

questions.q: Which IT Act section deals with cyber terrorism?
questions.e: Section 66F can carry imprisonment for life; 66C covers identity theft.

questions.q: Under the DPDP Act 2023, the maximum penalty for failing to take reasonable security safeguards is:
questions.e: Appeals from the Data Protection Board lie to TDSAT.

questions.q: SEBI's CSCRF is structured around which framework's functions?
questions.e: Governance plus Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover, with resilience emphasised.

questions.q: In digital forensics, the order of volatility says to collect first:
questions.e: Most volatile evidence disappears on power loss, so memory precedes disk.

questions.q: The only dependable control against ransomware destroying your backups is:
o: Immutable or offline backup copies that are restore-tested
questions.e: Continuous replication faithfully copies the encryption too.

questions.q: Zero trust is best summarised as:
o: Trust the internal network, verify externally
Never trust, always verify; assume breach
questions.e: NIST SP 800-207: verify explicitly, least-privilege access, assume breach.

questions.q: An IPS differs from an IDS because it:
o: Sits inline and can block traffic
questions.e: Being inline is what lets it prevent, and also what makes false positives costly.

questions.q: In IPsec, which protocol provides encryption as well as integrity?
questions.e: AH provides authentication and integrity only; ESP adds confidentiality.

questions.q: SEBI was given statutory status with effect from:
questions.e: It was set up as a non-statutory body in April 1988; the SEBI Act took effect from 30 January 1992.

questions.q: An appeal against a SEBI order lies to SAT within:
questions.e: A further appeal to the Supreme Court on a question of law lies within 60 days.

questions.q: SAT hears appeals from which of the following?
questions.e: RBI orders are not appealable to SAT - a frequently tested distinction.

questions.q: Which SEBI Act section empowers the Board to issue directions, including disgorgement?
questions.e: 11C is investigation, 15-I is adjudication and 24 covers offences.

questions.q: The open offer trigger under the SAST Regulations is acquisition of:
questions.e: Creeping acquisition permits up to 5% a year beyond that, and the open offer must be for at least 26%.

questions.q: Minimum public shareholding for a listed company under SCRR is:
questions.e: Rule 19A of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957.

questions.q: In a book-built issue, the cut-off price option is available to:
questions.e: QIBs and non-institutional investors must bid at a specific price.

questions.q: India completed its move to a T+1 rolling settlement cycle in:
questions.e: An optional same-day T+0 settlement beta followed in March 2024.

questions.q: Under the Depositories Act, the depository is the:
questions.e: The investor is the beneficial owner and holds all economic and voting rights.

questions.q: Which regulation governs corporate governance and disclosure by listed companies?
questions.e: ICDR covers issue of capital; SECC covers exchanges and clearing corporations.

questions.q: Insider trading penalties fall under which section of the SEBI Act?
questions.e: 15HA covers fraudulent and unfair trade practices.

questions.q: The monetary policy target for CPI inflation in India is:
questions.e: Set under the flexible inflation targeting framework adopted in 2016.

questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee has how many members?
questions.e: Three from RBI and three external members; the Governor has a casting vote.

questions.q: Which body is the unified regulator for GIFT City?
questions.e: IFSCA, established in 2020 and headquartered at Gandhinagar, covers banking, capital markets, insurance and funds.

questions.q: IOSCO, of which SEBI is a member, is headquartered at:
questions.e: BIS and FSB are at Basel; FATF and OECD at Paris.

questions.q: AIF Category III is characterised by:
o: Private equity and debt funds without leverage
Complex strategies that may employ leverage
questions.e: Category I is socially desirable sectors; Category II is PE and debt funds.

questions.q: A REIT must distribute at least what share of net distributable cash flows?
questions.e: At least 80% of assets must also be in completed, income-generating property.

questions.q: The minimum investment in a Portfolio Management Service is:
questions.e: Raised from Rs 25 lakh in 2020. AIFs require Rs 1 crore.

questions.q: Deposit insurance cover provided by DICGC per depositor per bank is:
questions.e: Raised from Rs 1 lakh in 2020.

questions.q: The Forward Markets Commission merged with SEBI in:
questions.e: On 28 September 2015, bringing commodity derivatives under SEBI.

questions.q: If in a code LIGHT is written as MJHIU, how is SOUND written?
questions.e: Each letter moves one step forward in the alphabet.

questions.q: Statements: All pens are books. Some books are red. Conclusion I: Some pens are red. Conclusion II: Some books are pens.
questions.e: Conversion of the universal affirmative gives II. I is only a possibility, not a certainty.

questions.q: Pointing to a photograph, a man says 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' The girl is his:
questions.e: His grandfather's only son is his own father, so the girl is his sister.

questions.q: If A > B, B >= C and C > D, which conclusion is definitely true?
questions.e: The chain A > B >= C > D gives A > D. The others break the chain direction.

questions.q: A man walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. How far is he from the start?
questions.e: He ends level with the start, displaced 3 km to the east.

questions.q: In a row of 40 students, Riya is 12th from the left. What is her position from the right?
questions.e: Position from right = total - position from left + 1 = 40 - 12 + 1 = 29.

questions.q: A sum doubles in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it triple?
questions.e: Doubling means interest equals the principal in 8 years, so 2x principal of interest takes 16 years.

questions.q: Successive discounts of 20% and 10% equal a single discount of:
A train 150 m long crosses a pole in 10 seconds. Its speed is:
questions.e: Crossing a pole means covering only the train length: 150/10 = 15 m/s, and 15 x 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.q: The difference between CI and SI on Rs 10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum is:
A can do a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together they finish it in:
Average speed for equal distances travelled at 40 km/h and 60 km/h is:
questions.e: Harmonic mean 2xy/(x+y) = 4800/100 = 48, not the arithmetic mean.

questions.q: The unit digit of 7^103 is:
questions.e: The cycle of 7 is 7, 9, 3, 1. 103 mod 4 = 3, so the third term, 3.

questions.q: In how many ways can 5 people sit around a circular table?
questions.e: Circular arrangements = (n-1)! = 4! = 24.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The list of items are on the desk.
The list of items is on the desk.
The list of item are on the desk.
List of items are on desk.
questions.e: The verb agrees with the subject 'list', not with the nearest noun 'items'.

questions.q: Neither the manager nor the officers ____ informed.
questions.e: With neither/nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'officers'.

questions.q: Which is correct?
o: He is more superior than me.
questions.e: Superior, inferior and prefer take 'to', never 'than'.

questions.q: 'Disinterested' correctly means:
questions.e: 'Uninterested' means bored; this pair is tested constantly.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'Walking to the station, the rain started falling heavily.'
questions.e: The introductory phrase must modify the subject; as written, the rain was walking.

questions.q: Which phrase is redundant?
questions.e: 'Return' already contains the sense of 'back'.
